subject: Islamic Studies
q: The literal meaning of the word ‘Islam’ is:
explanation: Islam comes from the root s-l-m and literally means submission, that is, surrendering oneself to the will of Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The literal meaning of ‘Iman’ is:
explanation: Iman literally means affirmation (tasdiq); in Islamic terms it is firm belief in the heart in all that the Holy Prophet (PBUH) brought from Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Tawhid’ means belief in:
explanation: Tawhid is the belief that Allah is One and without partner in His being, attributes and right to be worshipped; it is the foundation of Islamic faith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Belief in ‘Risalat’ means belief in:
o: Prophethood and the messengers of Allah
explanation: Risalat is belief that Allah sent messengers to guide mankind, culminating in the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The term ‘Akhirah’ refers to:
explanation: Akhirah is the Hereafter: resurrection, judgement and the eternal life that follows, one of the three fundamental beliefs of Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The opposite of Tawhid is:
explanation: Shirk means associating partners with Allah, which directly negates His Oneness; Nifaq is hypocrisy and Fisq is open disobedience.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A person who outwardly professes Islam but inwardly disbelieves is called:
explanation: A Munafiq (hypocrite) shows Islam outwardly while concealing disbelief; the Qur’an condemns hypocrisy severely, especially in Surah Al-Munafiqun.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The belief in Khatm-e-Nabuwwat means that:
o: No prophet will come after Muhammad (PBUH)
Every nation was sent a prophet
Prophethood can be attained through piety
explanation: The Qur’an calls the Holy Prophet (PBUH) Khatam-an-Nabiyyin, the Seal of the Prophets; prophethood ended with him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which angel brought revelation to the prophets?
explanation: Jibrail (Gabriel), called Ruh-ul-Amin in the Qur’an, conveyed Allah’s revelation to the prophets, including the Qur’an to the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which angel will blow the trumpet (Soor) to herald the Day of Resurrection?
explanation: Islamic tradition identifies Israfil as the angel who will blow the Soor, first bringing the world to an end and then raising the dead.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The angel who takes the souls of people at death is called in the Qur’an:
explanation: Surah As-Sajdah refers to the “Angel of Death” (Malak-ul-Maut) who takes souls; he is commonly known as Izrail.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is traditionally associated with:
o: Rain and the provision of sustenance
explanation: Mikail is named in Surah Al-Baqarah; Islamic tradition assigns him charge of rain and the provision (rizq) of creatures.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The angels who record the good and bad deeds of every person are called:
explanation: Surah Al-Infitar describes “noble scribes” (kiraman katibin) who know and record what people do; Hamalat-ul-Arsh are the bearers of the Throne.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Munkar and Nakir are the angels who:
o: Question the dead in the grave
explanation: According to Hadith, two angels called Munkar and Nakir question the deceased in the grave about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The angel in charge of Hell, named in the Qur’an, is:
explanation: In Surah Az-Zukhruf the people of Hell call out “O Malik”; Ridwan is traditionally regarded as the keeper of Paradise.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The intermediate state between death and the Day of Resurrection is called:
explanation: Barzakh literally means a barrier; the Qur’an (Al-Mu’minun) says a barrier stands before the dead until the Day they are raised. A‘raf is the height between Paradise and Hell.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Surah Al-Fatiha, ‘Yawm al-Din’ refers to:
o: The day of the first revelation
explanation: Allah is described as “Master of the Day of Recompense”; Din here means recompense, so Yawm al-Din is the Day of Judgement.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: On the Day of Judgement, the ‘Mizan’ refers to:
o: The scale on which deeds are weighed
explanation: The Qur’an states that just scales will be set up on the Day of Resurrection so that no soul is wronged in the least.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islamic belief, ‘al-Sirat’ on the Day of Judgement is:
o: The bridge over Hell that everyone must cross
explanation: Authentic Hadith describe the Sirat as a bridge set over Hell; the believers cross it according to their deeds.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islamic eschatology, ‘Hashr’ refers to:
o: The assembling of all creatures for Judgement
explanation: Hashr means gathering; after resurrection all people will be assembled before Allah for reckoning.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Belief in ‘Taqdir’ means belief in:
explanation: Taqdir (Qadr) is the belief that everything happens within Allah’s knowledge, will and decree; it is part of the articles of faith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The detailed declaration of faith, affirming belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, destiny and resurrection, is called:
explanation: Iman-e-Mufassal spells out the articles of faith in detail, whereas Iman-e-Mujmal is the brief summary statement of belief.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Tawrat was revealed to:
explanation: The Qur’an mentions the Tawrat (Torah) as the scripture given to Hazrat Musa (AS) for the Children of Israel.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Zabur was revealed to:
explanation: The Qur’an states, “And to Dawud We gave the Zabur” (the Psalms).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Injil was revealed to:
explanation: The Qur’an says Allah gave the Injil (Gospel) to Hazrat Isa (AS), containing guidance and light.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an mentions the ‘Suhuf’ (scrolls) of which two prophets?
explanation: Surah Al-A‘la closes with “the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa”; Surah An-Najm also refers to them.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Ismat-e-Anbiya’ refers to the belief that prophets are:
o: Able to know the unseen at will
explanation: Ismah means divine protection; prophets are safeguarded from sin so that their conduct can be followed as a model.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A supernatural act granted by Allah to a prophet as proof of his prophethood is called:
explanation: A Mu‘jizah is a miracle that others cannot match, given to a prophet to prove that he is sent by Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: An extraordinary event granted by Allah at the hands of a pious believer who is not a prophet is called:
explanation: Karamah is a mark of honour for a righteous believer; Irhas refers to signs before a prophet’s mission and Istidraj to apparent favours that lead a sinner gradually to ruin.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which is regarded as the everlasting miracle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
o: The flowing of water from his fingers
explanation: Other miracles were witnessed at particular times, but the Qur’an remains a living, inimitable challenge for all ages.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the commonly taught distinction, a Rasul differs from a Nabi in that a Rasul:
o: Is sent only to his own family
Is sent with a new Shariah or scripture
explanation: Every Rasul is a Nabi, but a Rasul is generally defined as one given a new law or book, while a Nabi may follow an earlier law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Al-Asma-ul-Husna’ refers to:
o: The most beautiful names of Allah
explanation: The Qur’an says “To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call on Him by them”; these names describe His attributes.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Islamic belief most directly establishes the equality of all human beings as servants of one Creator?
explanation: If there is one Creator and Lord of all, no person is lord over another; Tawhid therefore rejects superiority based on race, tribe or wealth.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Belief in the Hereafter chiefly develops in a believer:
o: A sense of accountability for every deed
explanation: Knowing that every deed will be judged makes a believer careful, just and responsible in private and public life.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Surah Luqman, Luqman tells his son that Shirk is:
explanation: Luqman advises, “Do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, Shirk is a great injustice (zulmun azim).”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The literal meaning of ‘Kufr’ is:
explanation: In Arabic a farmer who covers seed with soil is called kafir; Kufr is so named because it conceals and rejects the truth.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islamic usage, ‘Din’ denotes:
o: A complete way of life covering all spheres
explanation: Unlike the narrow sense of “religion” as private belief, Din embraces belief, worship, morality, law, economy and politics.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which of the following is one of the literal meanings of the Arabic word ‘Din’?
explanation: Din carries the meanings of obedience, a way of life and recompense, as in “Maliki Yawm al-Din” (Master of the Day of Recompense).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Hadith-e-Jibril, ‘Ihsan’ is defined as:
o: Worshipping Allah as though you see Him
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said Ihsan is to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Belief in ‘al-Ghayb’ means belief in:
o: Unseen realities made known through revelation
The findings of human reason alone
explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah praises those “who believe in the unseen”: Allah, angels, the Hereafter and other realities known only through revelation.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Shafa‘ah’ on the Day of Judgement means:
explanation: Shafa‘ah is intercession on behalf of others, which will take place only by Allah’s permission; the Holy Prophet (PBUH) will be the foremost intercessor.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Al-Kawthar, granted to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), is:
explanation: Surah Al-Kawthar mentions this gift, and authentic Hadith describe Kawthar as a river in Paradise promised to the Prophet (PBUH).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to Hadith, the highest level of Paradise is:
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said that when asking Allah for Paradise one should ask for Al-Firdaus, for it is the highest part of Paradise (Bukhari).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the Qur’an, ‘Ahl al-Kitab’ (People of the Book) mainly refers to:
explanation: The Qur’an uses Ahl al-Kitab for communities that received earlier scriptures, chiefly the Jews (Tawrat) and Christians (Injil).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Islamic concept of ‘Fitrah’ refers to:
o: The charity paid at the end of Ramadan
The innate disposition with which every person is born
The final stage of the soul
explanation: A Hadith states that every child is born upon the Fitrah, a natural inclination to recognise and worship the One Creator.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Ilham’ is best defined as:
o: Revelation brought by Jibrail to a prophet
Inspiration placed in the heart of a pious person
explanation: Ilham is inspiration from Allah to a non-prophet; unlike Wahi given to prophets, it is not a binding source of religious law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The primordial covenant in which the souls of mankind affirmed Allah as their Lord is known as:
explanation: Surah Al-A‘raf relates that Allah asked the progeny of Adam, “Am I not your Lord (alastu bi-rabbikum)?” and they replied, “Yes.”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Al-Qari‘ah, Al-Haqqah and Al-Ghashiyah are Qur’anic names of:
explanation: These names, meaning the Striking Calamity, the Inevitable Reality and the Overwhelming Event, describe the Day of Resurrection.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) called ‘Riya’ (showing off in worship):
explanation: In a Hadith (Musnad Ahmad) the Prophet (PBUH) said that what he feared most for his Ummah was minor shirk, and explained it as Riya.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Muslim who renounces Islam is termed:
explanation: Irtidad means turning back; a Murtad is one who abandons Islam after accepting it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’an, the ‘Amanah’ (Trust) that the heavens, the earth and the mountains declined to bear was taken up by:
explanation: Surah Al-Ahzab states that the heavens, earth and mountains shrank from the Trust, but man undertook it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’an, the jinn were created from:
explanation: Surah Ar-Rahman says the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, while man was created from clay.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to Hadith, angels were created from:
explanation: Sahih Muslim reports that angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire and Adam from clay.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’an, Iblis belonged to:
explanation: Surah Al-Kahf states that Iblis “was of the jinn” and disobeyed his Lord’s command to prostrate to Adam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an calls the Muslim Ummah ‘Ummatan Wasata’, meaning:
explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah describes Muslims as a just and moderate community, avoiding extremes, who bear witness over mankind.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’an, which is a distinctive feature of the message of Muhammad (PBUH) compared with earlier prophets?
o: It is addressed to the Arabs only
It was revealed in several languages
It is addressed to all mankind
explanation: Earlier prophets were sent to particular nations, but the Qur’an says the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was sent to all of mankind.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The term ‘Bid‘ah’ literally means:
explanation: Bid‘ah literally means something newly originated; in religious usage it refers to an innovation in matters of Din.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic phrase ‘We make no distinction between any of His messengers’ means that Muslims:
o: Regard all messengers as having the same law
Believe in all the messengers of Allah
Follow the scriptures of every messenger
Believe only in the last messenger
explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah requires faith in every messenger; rejecting any one of them is rejecting the message of Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The branch of Islamic learning that deals with articles of faith and their rational defence is:
explanation: Ilm-ul-Kalam (scholastic theology) explains and defends Islamic beliefs with reasoned argument; Fiqh deals with practical rulings.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Kalima-e-Shahadat bears witness to:
o: The Day of Judgement and resurrection
The angels and the revealed books
The Oneness of Allah and the messengership of Muhammad (PBUH)
explanation: The Shahadah testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad (PBUH) is His servant and Messenger; it is the entry into Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The word ‘Aqidah’ (creed) is derived from a root meaning:
explanation: Aqidah comes from ‘aqd, a firm knot; it denotes beliefs held firmly in the heart.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Correct belief in Taqdir encourages a believer to:
o: Strive fully and accept the outcome with patience
explanation: Islam joins effort with trust: a believer uses all lawful means and then accepts Allah’s decree without despair or arrogance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to Islamic belief, angels:
o: Have free will like human beings
Always obey Allah and never disobey Him
explanation: Surah At-Tahrim describes angels who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic word ‘Rabb’ primarily means:
o: The Lord who creates, nurtures and sustains
explanation: Rabb denotes the Master who brings creation into being and nurtures it stage by stage; Rahman, Ghafur and Malik are other names.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Surah Al-Ikhlas, Allah is described as ‘Al-Samad’, which means:
o: The Eternal Refuge on whom all depend
explanation: Al-Samad is the Self-Sufficient Master whom all creation needs while He needs none.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Muslims believe that the scriptures revealed before the Qur’an:
o: Were from Allah but were not preserved in their original form
Remain binding in place of the Qur’an
explanation: Belief in all revealed books is an article of faith, but the Qur’an teaches that earlier texts were altered and that it is the final, preserved guidance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Al-Ba‘th ba‘d al-Maut’ means:
explanation: It is the belief, stated in Iman-e-Mufassal, that Allah will raise all the dead to life for judgement.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islamic belief, ‘Al-A‘raf’ is:
o: The elevated place between Paradise and Hell
The pond of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
explanation: Surah Al-A‘raf describes people on the heights between Paradise and Hell who recognise the dwellers of both by their marks.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Those who will receive their record of deeds in their right hand are called in the Qur’an:
explanation: Surah Al-Waqi‘ah and Al-Haqqah describe the Companions of the Right, who receive their record in the right hand and are successful.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first revelation came to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in:
explanation: The first verses were revealed in the Cave of Hira on Jabal-un-Nur; the Cave of Thawr was the refuge during the Hijrah.
